'''Carolin Susan Crawford''' is a British [[science communication|communicator of science]] and [[astrophysicist]]. She is an emeritus member of the [[Institute of Astronomy, Cambridge]]<ref name=whoswho/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/reporter/2010-11/special/03/section1.shtml#heading2-8|title=Fellow of the Colleges: Emmanuel College|work=[[Cambridge University Reporter]] No 3: Fellows of the Colleges|publisher=Cambridge University|date=7 October 2010|accessdate=24 August 2011}}</ref> and an emeritus  [[fellow]] of [[Emmanuel College, Cambridge]].<ref name=emma>{{cite web|url=https://www.emma.cam.ac.uk/contact/fellows/?id=209|title=Dr Carolin Crawford - Fellows - Contact - Emmanuel College, Cambridge|website=www.emma.cam.ac.uk}}</ref><ref name="CrawfordHatch2005">{{cite journal|last1=Crawford|first1=C. S.|last2=Hatch|first2=N. A.|last3=Fabian|first3=A. C.|last4=Sanders|first4=J. S.|title=The extended H -emitting filaments surrounding NGC 4696, the central galaxy of the Centaurus cluster|journal=Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society|volume=363|issue=1|year=2005|pages=216–222|issn=0035-8711|doi=10.1111/j.1365-2966.2005.09463.x|doi-access=free |arxiv=astro-ph/0507627|s2cid=13894970 }}</ref>

==Education==
Crawford studied the [[Mathematical Tripos]] and received a [[Bachelor of Arts]] honours degree in mathematics at [[Newnham College, Cambridge]] in 1985. In 1988 she received her [[PhD]]<ref name=crawphd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Cambridge|url=https://copac.jisc.ac.uk/id/9514519?style=html|title=The detection of distant cooling flows.|first=Carolin Susan|last=Crawford|date=1988|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.293490}}|website=jisc.ac.uk|oclc=53538712|accessdate=9 November 2018|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20181109234911/https://copac.jisc.ac.uk/id/9514519?style=html|archivedate=9 November 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> for research undertaken at the [[Institute of Astronomy, Cambridge]] on [[cooling flow]]s.

==Career and research==
After her PhD, Crawford progressed through a series of [[postdoctoral]] and [[research fellow]]ships at [[Balliol College, Oxford]], the Institute of Astronomy, [[Trinity Hall, Cambridge]] and [[Newnham College, Cambridge]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr Carolin Crawford {{!}} Institute of Astronomy |url=https://www.ast.cam.ac.uk/people/Carolin.Crawford |access-date=2022-03-01 |website=www.ast.cam.ac.uk}}</ref> From 1996 to 2007 she held a [[Royal Society University Research Fellow]]ship.<ref name="gc_cv_crawford">{{Cite web |url=http://www-xray.ast.cam.ac.uk/~csc/newcv/Crawford%20short%20CV.pdf |title=Curriculum Vitae: Carolin Crawford |publisher=[[Gresham College]] |accessdate=2015-07-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303225905/http://www-xray.ast.cam.ac.uk/~csc/newcv/Crawford%20short%20CV.pdf |archive-date=2016-03-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2004 she was appointed a [[Fellow]] and College [[Lecturer]] at Emmanuel College, Cambridge, where was also the undergraduate admissions tutor for the [[Physical Science]]s. She held this position in conjunction with her role as Public Astronomer at the Institute of Astronomy, which she first took on in 2005.<ref name="gc_cv_crawford" />

She served as [[Gresham Professor of Astronomy]] at [[Gresham College]] from 2011 to 2015, a position in which she delivered free public lectures on astronomy and astrophysics in the [[City of London]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gresham.ac.uk/gresham-college-press-release-13062011 |title=Gresham College Press Release 13/06/2011 &#124; Gresham College |publisher=[[Gresham College]] |date=2011-06-13 |accessdate=2014-07-18 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140725171105/http://www.gresham.ac.uk/gresham-college-press-release-13062011 |archivedate=2014-07-25 }}</ref>

Crawford's "primary research interests are in combining [[X-ray astronomy|X-ray]], optical and near-infrared observations to study the physical processes occurring around massive galaxies at the core of [[Galaxy groups and clusters|clusters of galaxies]]. In particular, she observes the complex interplay between the hot intra-cluster medium, filaments of warm ionized gas, cold [[molecular clouds]], [[star formation]] and the radio plasma flowing out from the [[supermassive black hole|central supermassive black hole]]."<ref>{{cite web|author=Anon |url=http://www.emma.cam.ac.uk/teaching/fellows/display/?fellow=209 |title=Emmanuel College &#124; Contact &#124; Fellows |publisher=Emma.cam.ac.uk |date= |accessdate=2014-07-18}}</ref>

===Outreach and awards===
Crawford delivers public lectures, talks, workshops and debates throughout the UK and beyond on wide range of topics within astronomy. She regularly delivers such science outreach presentations to over 4,000 people annually.
She is a regular in broadcast media, with numerous appearances on programmes such as ''[[In Our Time (BBC Radio 4)|In Our Time]]'' and ''Home Planet'' on [[BBC Radio 4]].

In 2009 Crawford was recognised for her outstanding abilities at science communication by a [[Women of Outstanding Achievement Award]] by the UK Resource Centre for Women in Science, Engineering and Technology, presented for “communication of science with a contribution to society.”<ref>{{Cite web|title=Women of Outstanding Achievement |url=https://www.wisecampaign.org.uk/wise-awards/women-of-outstanding-achievement |publisher=[[WISE Campaign]] |accessdate=2015-07-30 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150908111820/https://www.wisecampaign.org.uk/wise-awards/women-of-outstanding-achievement |archivedate=2015-09-08 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Women of Outstanding Achievement 2009 booklet |url=https://www.wisecampaign.org.uk/resources/2009/11/women-of-outstanding-achievement-2009-booklet |date=2 November 2009 |publisher=[[WISE Campaign]] |accessdate=2015-07-30 |archive-date=19 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150919162003/https://www.wisecampaign.org.uk/resources/2009/11/women-of-outstanding-achievement-2009-booklet |url-status=dead }}</ref>
